notes: Settlement 2026-11-07: reliefs (disability exclusion, Schedule I Calculation B Lines 7a and 7b): covers: A said all_income, B said other_income; income_test.measure.base: A said federal_agi, B said household_income. PDF page 66, Line 7a and 7b: 'Income not to exceed $10,000 is excludable in computing DC gross income for persons determined by the Social Security Administration to be totally and permanently disabled ... and whose annual household adjusted gross income is less than $100,000. Household income includes income received by all household members in the year, even income excluded from federal adjusted gross income.' The exclusion is of income of any kind, so covers all_income (A; brief rule 14); the test is on household income, not the filer's federal AGI, so base household_income (B). Both readers agreed on cap 10000, cap_per return, effect removes, threshold 100000; kept.

Settlement 2026-11-07: reliefs (Line 10, taxable Social Security and tier 1 railroad retirement): A wrote a relief entry, B wrote none (only social_security.treatment). PDF page 20, Line 10 'Taxable amount of social security and tier 1 railroad retirement ... Enter the amount from 1040 or 1040-SR' and D-40 form page 2, Line 10, under 'Subtractions from DC Income', print it; kept, because it is the only line that carries tier 1 railroad retirement.

Settlement 2026-11-07: indexing: A wrote entries for brackets and standard_deduction (not_stated), B wrote only all_other. The booklet says nothing about inflation adjustment of either (PDF page 5 'Income Tax Rate Table - For taxable years beginning January 1, 2022'; PDF page 13 Standard Deduction; PDF page 20 Calculation I); brief rule 8 asks for an entry per figure only when the booklet says something about it, so A's two extra entries are dropped and all_other (not_stated) is kept.

Settlement 2026-11-07: standard deduction (both readers agree; checked against the rendered pages): PDF page 4 'DC Basic Standard Deduction ... For tax year 2025, those amounts are: $15,000 for single filers, dependent filers and married/registered domestic partner filers filing separately; $22,500 for head of household filers; and $30,000 for married/registered domestic partners filing jointly and qualifying widow(er) with dependent child filers'; PDF page 13 'Standard Deduction' prints the same three amounts and adds 'married/registered domestic partners filing separately on the same return are allowed a standard deduction of $30,000'; the PDF page 7 filing requirements chart prints the same amounts; Schedule S Calculation G-1 (PDF page 51) line a 'Basic standard deduction amount', line g 'Multiply $1,600 ($2,000 if your filing status is single, head of household, or dependent claimed by someone else and are not married) by the number on Line f'. The pypdf text of page 13 is garbled ('$£x,000', '$22,x00') but the docling text of page 4 and the rendered page read 15,000 and 22,500.

Settlement 2026-11-07: page numbers: B cited the docling page markers (Schedule S page 46, Schedule I pages 58 and 60), A the PDF page numbers (51, 64, 66). The PDF has 105 pages and the docling conversion only 96 page markers, so docling's markers drift after page 20; the cites here use the PDF page numbers (pypdf, checked by rendering pages 4, 13 and 51).

Tax rate schedule: Calculation I/Tax Rate Schedule (PDF page 20) and the Income Tax Rate Table on PDF page 5 print one schedule for every filing status: 4% not over 10,000; $400 plus 6% over 10,000; $2,200 plus 6.5% over 40,000; $3,500 plus 8.5% over 60,000; $19,650 plus 9.25% over 250,000; $42,775 plus 9.75% over 500,000; $91,525 plus 10.75% over 1,000,000. The booklet prints no separate schedule for married filing separately or head of household, so only single and married_joint are given (the same schedule). The cumulative amounts check (400 = 4% of 10,000; 2,200 = 400 + 6% of 30,000; 3,500; 19,650; 42,775; 91,525).

D-40 Line 20: tax on Line 19 taxable income of $100,000 or less is read from the tax tables (PDF pages 94-103), above that from Calculation I. Three table rows were checked against the schedule: 21,650-21,699 tax 1,101 (PDF page 96; schedule at 21,675: 1,100.50); 50,950-50,999 tax 2,913 (PDF page 99; schedule 2,913.38); 82,350-82,399 tax 5,401 (PDF page 102; schedule 5,401.88). brackets.derivation is not used because the schedule itself is printed.

Standard deduction is per return; the 'dependent filer' status (15,000) and 'married filing separately on the same return' (30,000) have no schema status key and are described here only. Married filing separately on separate returns: 15,000.

Additional standard deduction (PDF page 4, page 13, Schedule S Calculation G-1 lines b-g, PDF page 51): $1,600 for each of age 65 or over and blind, for the filer and (joint or same-return filers) the spouse; $2,000 if the filing status is single, head of household, or dependent claimed by someone else and not married. 'If you were born before January 2, 1961, you are considered to be age 65 at the end of 2025.' Recorded as two per-person entries (age 65, blind); 2,000 keyed to single and head_of_household, 1,600 to married_joint, married_separate and qualifying_surviving_spouse (the qualifying widow(er) is not in the 2,000 list). Married filing separately (not on the same return): the spouse's additional amount only if the spouse had no gross income, is not filing and cannot be claimed as a dependent (PDF page 4).

The booklet prints no personal exemption and no dependent exemption amount for 2025 (Calculation G-1 line i counts dependents but no amount per dependent is printed; 'exemption' appears elsewhere only for health coverage).

Standard deduction condition: 'You are not entitled to the standard deduction if you itemize on your federal return. You are entitled to the itemized deductions excluding the state and local taxes and subject to the DC 5% limitation' (PDF page 13, quoting D.C. Code 47-1803.04(b)); D-40 Line 17 'You must take the same type of deduction on your DC return as you took on your federal return' (PDF page 20). DC itemized deductions are reduced by 5% of DC AGI over $200,000 ($100,000 married filing separately); not recorded as a deduction entry because they have no fixed amount.

Federal Schedule 1-A additional deductions (no tax on tips, overtime, car loan interest, Enhanced Deduction for Seniors) are not allowed (PDF page 4); they are below federal AGI and do not change the DC starting point.

Social Security: exempt. D-40 Line 10 subtracts the 'Taxable amount of social security and tier 1 railroad retirement' (form page 2, Line 10, under 'Subtractions from DC Income'; booklet PDF page 20 Line 10 'Enter the amount from 1040 or 1040-SR'), so all Social Security in federal AGI is subtracted. Tier 2 railroad retirement is not named on Line 10 or anywhere else in the booklet (neither covered nor excluded).

Pensions, IRA and employer-plan distributions, Roth conversions: PDF page 19, Line 4: 'Enter the amount from 1040, 1040-SR, 1040-NR, or 1040-NR-EZ. Include your taxable portion of pension/annuity in your federal adjusted gross income.' No retirement-income exclusion or subtraction for private pensions, IRA distributions, employer-plan distributions, Roth conversions, military retirement or annuities was found on D-40 Lines 8-14, Schedule I Calculation B Lines 1-15 (PDF page 64) or their instructions (PDF pages 20, 66); not found in the booklet, so these are taxed as part of federal AGI.

Government pensions of DC and the federal government: the only government-pension line is D-40 Line 12 'DC and federal government survivor benefits' (PDF page 20): 'If you are an annuitant's survivor and 62 years of age or older as of December 31, 2025, enter the total survivor benefits (do not include Social Security survivor benefits).' Recorded under public_pension; no cap printed. A retiree's own DC or federal government pension: no subtraction found in the booklet (taxed via federal AGI).

Pensions from other states' governments (brief rule 15a), including a New York State pension: not found in the booklet. Line 12 names only 'DC and federal government' survivor benefits, and no line names another state's government pension, so such a pension stays in federal AGI and is taxed; public_pension_other_state is in no entry's covers.

Disability: Calculation B Line 2 also allows a disability income exclusion from Form D-2440 (PDF page 66); its amounts and rules are not in the booklet, so no entry. The Line 7a exclusion: the booklet does not say whether the $10,000 is per person or per return (form line 7a 'Exclusion of up to $10,000 for DC residents'); recorded per return as both readers did.

Interest and dividends on obligations or securities of the United States or its agencies or instrumentalities, to the extent included in federal gross income, are subtracted (Calculation B Line 1, PDF pages 64 and 66); no cap printed.

Municipal bonds: interest on obligations of other states and their political subdivisions is included in DC gross income starting 2025 (Calculation A Line 7 addback); interest on obligations of DC, a US territory, DC Water, WMATA and DCHFA remains exempt (PDF pages 2, 4 and 65).

Capital gains: no separate rate or deduction. Gain excluded federally under IRC 1202 (qualified small business stock) is added back to DC income (PDF page 4); capital loss limited to $3,000 ($1,500 married filing separately) (PDF page 19). capital_gains is empty.
Unemployment insurance benefits provided by the federal government, the District or any other state are excluded (D-40 Line 13, PDF page 20); not a retirement income kind, not recorded as a relief.
Filing threshold: from 2025 DC has its own filing threshold equal to its standard deduction (PDF page 7 chart).
Part-year residents have separate rules (Calculation C, D-40 Line 8); not read into this record.
No surtax and no recapture of lower brackets found in the booklet; surtaxes and recapture are empty lists meaning not found.
